units.label: 1(a)
units.summary: Complete a structure diagram showing the component parts of the function room booking problem.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark decomposition of an unfamiliar scenario into components.

units.label: 1(b)
units.summary: State the purpose of an integrated development environment.
units.difficulty_basis: 1-mark recall of IDE purpose.

units.label: 1(c)
units.summary: State two programming constructs and give a context-specific example of each in the booking program.
units.difficulty_basis: 4 marks; recall of constructs plus applying each to the scenario.

units.label: 1(d)
units.summary: State two test strategies that could be used.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark recall of named test strategies.

units.label: 1(e)
units.summary: State two software development methodologies that could be considered.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark recall of named methodologies.

units.label: 1(f)
units.summary: Explain two benefits of using reusable components when writing code.
units.difficulty_basis: 4 marks; two benefits each needing an explanation.

units.label: 2(a)(i)
units.summary: Explain why a loop-based validation is more effective than a selection-based one for checking telephone number length.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark explanation comparing two given code versions.

units.label: 2(a)(ii)
units.summary: State two further procedures for a described program extension, giving a name and purpose for each.
units.difficulty_basis: 4 marks; identifying sub-procedures for an application context.

units.label: 2(a)(iii)
units.summary: State the difference between passing parameters by reference and by value.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark recall of parameter passing difference.

units.label: 2(b)
units.summary: Discuss how modularity lets a team of programmers work together effectively on one program.
units.difficulty_basis: 9-mark extended response requiring a balanced discussion and judgment.

units.label: 3(a)
units.summary: Show the first pass of a bubble sort on a five-item list with each comparison.
units.difficulty_basis: 4-mark trace of a standard algorithm on given data.

units.label: 3(b)(i)
units.summary: Identify a line in the given bubble sort where a decision is taken.
units.difficulty_basis: 1-mark identification from given code.

units.label: 3(b)(ii)
units.summary: Identify the parameter name used by the bubble sort procedure.
units.difficulty_basis: 1-mark identification from given code.

units.label: 3(b)(iii)
units.summary: Describe the purpose of the temporary variable in the bubble sort procedure.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark routine description of a swap variable in familiar code.

units.label: 3(b)(iv)
units.summary: Describe the purpose of the sorted flag variable in the bubble sort procedure.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark routine description of a flag in familiar code.

units.label: 4(a)
units.summary: Explain why the assignment operator rather than comparison operator is used on a given line.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark explanation of assignment versus comparison.

units.label: 4(b)
units.summary: State the values printed by the procedure for an even input.
units.difficulty_basis: 1-mark short trace of given code.

units.label: 4(c)
units.summary: State the values printed by the procedure for an odd input.
units.difficulty_basis: 1-mark short trace of given code.

units.label: 4(d)
units.summary: Describe the purpose of the MOD operator on a given line.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark recall of modulo use.

units.label: 5(a)
units.summary: Describe how a linear search could find the first available booking slot.
units.difficulty_basis: 3-mark description of a standard algorithm applied to a scenario.

units.label: 5(b)
units.summary: Write a function that finds the first free slot in a two-dimensional array or returns -1.
units.difficulty_basis: 7-mark original algorithm with loop, array access and returns for an unfamiliar problem.

units.label: 5(c)
units.summary: State why a function rather than a procedure is used for the validity check.
units.difficulty_basis: 1-mark recall of function versus procedure.

units.label: 6(a)
units.summary: Describe how the procedure name is used differently on the calling line and the definition line.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark call versus definition distinction.

units.label: 6(b)
units.summary: Explain why a global variable always prints zero after the procedure has run.
units.difficulty_basis: 2-mark trace-based reasoning about global variable state.

units.label: 6(c)
units.summary: Explain why a string conversion is used in the output lines.
units.difficulty_basis: 3-mark explanation of type casting for concatenation.
